input.brief: Safedeal is an escrow-protected marketplace for verified gaming accounts, game keys, in-game currency and digital goods, for gamers who need trust and instant delivery

direction.name: The specimen catalogue
direction.idea: Present what is on offer the way a field guide presents birds: each item alone on a flat colour, same scale, same angle, named plainly. A bakery's pastries become specimens and the specimens become the menu. A furniture maker's chairs each get their own colour tile. The format flatters ordinary objects because it treats each as worth looking at, and it replaces both the feature grid and the product-card grid with something that has a point of view.
direction.composition: Hero: a left-aligned statement of what this is (5–7vw, upper-left) beside or above a tight cluster of four to seven specimen tiles of different sizes arranged as a loose mosaic that runs off the right edge. Each tile is a flat colour square or 4:5 rectangle with one photograph centred on it, no border, 8–12px gaps. The main section is the catalogue itself: a grid of tiles in which each item has its name and one fact set beneath the tile in the text face, aligned left to the tile edge. Tile colours rotate through three or four fields from the palette. One tile in every six or seven is double size. Supporting sections (about, how to order) are plain text on the ground colour, kept short.
direction.typography: Friendly and plain. Item names at 18–22px in medium weight, facts beneath in the soft ink. One big statement in the hero; no other display type.
direction.colour: The tiles are the colour: three or four flat fields from the palette, repeated in a steady rotation. Ground stays neutral.
direction.imagery: Photographs of single items on plain backgrounds, all cropped to sit at the same apparent size within their tile. On light tiles, `mix-blend-mode: multiply` removes white studio backgrounds. If the subject's own item photographs are missing, use the dealt set and say so.
direction.richness: Rhythm of colour tiles and the pleasure of comparing like with like.
direction.pitfalls: It needs at least six items that can be shown as objects; with three it is a feature row. Keep labels outside the tiles. No shadows under the objects, no hover lift.

hero.name: Specimen wall, docked panel
hero.blueprint: There is no header and no display headline: the whole viewport is a wall of specimens. Square tiles of about 112px (7.8vw) with 8px gaps fill the screen edge to edge in eight rows; alternate rows shift half a tile sideways so the wall reads as brickwork, and tiles at every edge are cropped by the viewport (overflow: hidden on the section). Each tile is a flat fill, rotating through three palette colours, holding one cut-out item at 60% of the tile, centred, with mix-blend-mode: multiply on light fills. A solid panel in the ink colour, 800px wide (columns 4-9) and about 170px tall with square corners, is docked at the bottom centre, 24px above the bottom edge, covering the tiles behind it. Inside, on 28px padding: the sentence that says what this is at 24px semibold on the left across two lines, the single action as a filled rectangle in the paper colour on the right, and beneath them a row holding the wordmark and four text links at 15px. Nothing else overlays the wall.
hero.mobile: Tiles become 22vw squares with 6px gaps, four and a half per row, still offset as brickwork and cropped at both sides. The panel turns into a full-width block fixed to the bottom of the first screen, about a third of its height: the sentence at 6vw on two lines, the action full width beneath it, the wordmark and links in one wrapped row at 14px. The wall fills everything above.
hero.headline: No display line: one plain sentence of up to 56 characters inside the panel names what the items are.

type.note: A soft geometric sans with wide round letters and relaxed joins, warm at semibold and easy at text size. Suits consumer apps, community products, cafes and small friendly brands.

palette.name: Sand and moss
palette.note: Sand grey holds the page with charcoal type, and one deep leaf-green band may close it. Moss green is reserved for buttons; brighter greens and blues arrive only through photographs.

motion.name: Index with preview
motion.description: Rows of text are the navigation through the work; pointing at a row brings up its image in one fixed frame and dims the other rows. On touch screens each row shows its image inline instead. Fast and exact (about 240ms crossfade), no lag behind the pointer. Recipe: 'List with image preview' in references/motion.md.

sections.name: Two objects, two fields
sections.blueprint: Two panels side by side, each 50vw wide and 92svh tall, in two different flat tones from the palette, meeting on a clean vertical edge with no gap. Each panel is dominated by one cut-out object photograph scaled to 130–150% of the panel's width and positioned so the panel's top edge crops it: the reader sees the lower two-thirds of the object, very close. On light panels use mix-blend-mode: multiply to lose a white studio background. Along the bottom of each panel, 28px in from the edges, one row: the name at 20px medium and a price or fact at 17px on the left; on the right, two small rectangular actions, one filled with ink and one with paper. Nothing sits in the middle of a panel. The heading, two to four words at 32–40px, is set at the top-left of the first panel only, in the empty corner beside the object.
sections.mobile: Panels stack, each 78svh tall, the object scaled to 150% of the width and cut by the top and right edges. The bottom row becomes two lines: name and fact, then the two actions side by side at full width. The heading sits top-left on the first panel at 26px.

sections.name: Tiles that grow
sections.blueprint: Order is carried by size. Three flat colour tiles stand in one row, bottom-aligned (align-items: end) with 10px gaps, each larger than the one before: columns 1–3 at 30vh tall, columns 4–7 at 44vh, columns 8–12 at 60vh. Each tile holds one photograph of the subject at that stage (raw, in progress, finished), centred and scaled so the object grows from tile to tile; on light tiles mix-blend-mode: multiply removes a white studio background. One palette colour per tile. Text sits under the tiles, outside them, aligned to each tile's left edge: a stage name at 20px medium whose wording carries the order ('Picked', 'Pressed', 'Poured') and two lines at 16px in the soft ink. The heading, two to four words at 40–52px, occupies the empty ground above the two smaller tiles, top-aligned with the tallest tile. A fourth stage is possible with spans of 2, 3, 3 and 4 columns.
sections.mobile: Tiles stack in order and grow in height instead: 34vw, 46vw and 62vw tall, each at full width. The name and text sit under each tile at 18px and 16px. The heading comes first at 30px. 28px between stages.

sections.name: The printed guest list
sections.blueprint: Names are printed on a card, the way a programme lists its patrons or an invitation its hosts. On a contrasting flat ground, a paper-coloured panel about 56% of the viewport wide with 5:7 proportions sits centred and rotated by one or two degrees; the section is shorter than the card and clips it with `overflow: hidden`, so the card is cut by the bottom edge rather than framed whole. Inside, 56px padding. At the top, a centred heading of two to four words at 28px. Below it the names run as centred lines at 20–22px with leading 1.7, several names to a line, separated by middots with a non-breaking space either side. One photograph may be tipped in between the heading and the names: 16:9, the full inner width, square corners. The card is a plain filled shape with no outline.
sections.mobile: The card becomes 92% of the screen wide, keeps a one-degree tilt and is still cut off by the section's bottom edge. Heading at 22px, names at 17px with two names to a line. Padding drops to 28px, and the tipped-in photograph keeps the full inner width.

sections.name: Stepped figure tiles
sections.blueprint: Three figures on three tiles that refuse to line up. A tall tile in the accent colour fills columns 1–6 and is 70vh high; it holds one figure at clamp(56px, 5.4vw, 92px) in its top-left corner, 28px in, and its caption at 17px in its bottom-left corner, with empty colour between. On the right, an ink-coloured tile in columns 7–9 starts 14vh lower and is 44vh high: a paper-coloured figure top-left, a caption along its bottom edge. A third tile in a mid tone takes columns 10–12, starts 26vh down and is 34vh high, with the same internal layout. Gaps are 8px. The unequal heights leave notches of bare ground above and below the right-hand tiles; the heading, two to four words at 28–36px, sits in the upper notch on column 7. If the page has a motif, cut one corner of each tile to its geometry with clip-path.
sections.mobile: The tall tile comes first, at full width and 56vw high, with its figure at 15vw. The two smaller tiles follow side by side with a 6px gap, the right one starting 32px lower than the left, each with its figure at 11vw and its caption at the bottom. The heading sits above at 26px.

sections.name: Quotes on paper slips
sections.blueprint: A heading of two to four words at about 3vw sits top-left in columns 1–6. Beneath it three paper slips fan across columns 2–11 on a contrasting flat ground: each is a filled paper-coloured panel about 300px wide, of three different lengths (440, 520 and 600px), rotated −4, 2 and 5 degrees and overlapping its neighbour by roughly 40px. The top and bottom edges of each slip are zigzag tears cut with `clip-path: polygon()`. On a slip, from the top: the speaker's name centred at 18px bold, the role on one line, a square greyscale photograph of the speaker 120px wide, then the quotation at 16px in the text face, left-aligned with 24px padding. The longest slip runs past the bottom of the section, which clips it with `overflow: hidden`, so the slips look freshly printed rather than laid out as cards.
sections.mobile: One slip per row, each 78% of the screen wide and kept rotated by two or three degrees in alternating directions, the first hugging the left margin, the second the right, each overlapping the one above by 32px. The heading sits above at 8vw on two lines.

sections.name: Tabbed index cards
sections.blueprint: Questions are filed like cards in a drawer. A heading of two to four words at about 4vw sits in columns 3–10. Beneath it, in the same columns, five or six filled panels are stacked so that each overlaps the one above, leaving 96px of every card showing. Each card has a tab on its top edge, 200px wide and 40px tall, stepping right by 150px per card, cut with `clip-path: polygon()` so card and tab are one filled shape. The cards rotate through two or three palette colours. The tab carries the topic in one or two words at 16px; the visible strip under it shows the question at 20px medium. Choosing a card expands it to show the answer at 17px over at most 50ch and pushes the cards below it down. One card is open at a time; the first is open on load.
sections.mobile: Cards run full width with the same overlap, 88px of each showing. Tabs shrink to 120px wide and step right by 48px per card. The open card expands in place with its answer at 16px and 20px padding, and the heading leads at 9vw.

sections.name: Three photographs, then a field
sections.blueprint: Two parts with no gap between them. First, a strip of three photographs butted edge to edge across the full viewport, each one third wide and 40svh tall, `object-fit: cover`, no gutters and no captions; give all three the same treatment. Directly beneath, a band in one flat palette colour, about 44svh tall. In the band, columns 1–7: the closing statement at 26–30px over three lines in the band's assigned ink, with exactly one phrase underlined by a 4px bar (`text-decoration-thickness: 4px; text-underline-offset: 6px`), and that phrase is the link; two lines at 16px follow 32px lower. In the lower-right corner, columns 11–12, a small portrait photograph (4:5, about 150px wide) sits 40px from the band's edges: the person who will answer. There is no button; the underlined phrase is the action.
sections.mobile: The strip becomes one full-width photograph at 4:3 with the other two side by side beneath it at half width each, still gutterless. The band follows: statement at 22px, the two small lines, and the portrait at 96px wide in the bottom-right corner.

sections.name: The mark, built large
sections.blueprint: On a flat colour field, the brand closes the page as a construction rather than as set type. Across the full content width and about 34svh tall, the wordmark is built from blocks: each letter is knocked out of its own solid rectangle in a palette colour, the rectangles differ in height (60–100% of the band) and butt together with 4px gaps, bottoms on one line. Where the project has a simple geometric mark or motif, enlarge that instead, drawn as inline SVG from flat rectangles, circles and quarter-arcs with the same 4px gaps. Below, 56px lower: four columns of plain links at 15px across columns 1–8, and two addresses or contact lines in columns 9–12. A last row carries the copyright at the left and one small filled button at the right. Space and the block construction do all the separating.
sections.mobile: The block wordmark spans the full width at about 22svh tall; a long name breaks into two rows of blocks. Link columns go two across at 15px, contact lines beneath at full width, then copyright and the small button on one row.

references.name: Madie
references.idea: A burgundy-and-cream bakery brand in which the madeleines themselves, cut out like specimens, become the menu.
references.hero: A dark, warm photograph (iced coffee with a logo sticker and a glazed madeleine on a wooden counter, burgundy tiles behind) fills a rounded-corner frame inset 20px from every edge on a cream page; the subject sits right of centre. In the left column, starting 42% down: a small star-rating line, then a three-line uppercase headline at 5vw in a heavy geometric sans, the first two lines outline-only and the third solid cream, a three-line paragraph, and a row with a pink pill button and an underlined text link. Top-left: menu icon and script logo. Top-right: a three-language pill toggle. Bottom-right: a circular text badge.
references.type: Dazzle, a heavy geometric uppercase, for headlines at 72px, used both solid and as an outline stroke; Cottorway, a slightly wide geometric sans, for 14px body and for a light italic accent word. A brush-script logo. Tracked capitals near 10px for labels.
references.colour: #f6efe6 #3d0012 #5c0a23 #ff99d3 #160b0a #e8a530 — Cream and deep burgundy alternate by section across wavy boundaries. Bubblegum pink is reserved for buttons, the active filter pill and carousel arrows; the product cut-outs supply every other colour.
references.imagery: A moody warm-graded hero photo; individual madeleines shot from above and cut out with soft shadows as small menu thumbnails; white line drawings (dog in beret, cafe table); rounded photo cards stacked at a tilt; a map redrawn in burgundy.
references.layout: Centred intro, a left-anchored story block on burgundy, then a two-column menu inside a container about 60% of the width. Section edges are curved waves rather than straight lines. Rounded frames and a sticky header with filter pills recur throughout.

sections.description: Cream field, everything centred. A tiny tracked-capitals label flanked by two short rules, then a two-line heading: the first line outlined uppercase in burgundy at about 4.5vw, the second a lowercase light italic of the body sans, solid. Three short paragraphs at 13px follow in a column about 45% wide. The section ends in a burgundy wave rising from the bottom, with a white line-drawn dog perched on the curve.

Burgundy field patterned with a faint tone-on-tone repeat of the logo. Left: a white line illustration, a three-line paragraph with bold phrases, two round pink arrow buttons and a slide counter. Right: a stack of portrait photo cards with rounded corners, the top one tilted a few degrees and the others fanned behind it. The bottom edge curves back to cream.

A sticky row of three pill filters beside the logo, the active one filled pink. Each category has an outlined uppercase label at left, an item count at far right and a hairline beneath. Items run in two columns: a 60px cut-out madeleine at left, then a bold uppercase name and a two-to-three-line italic description; some carry a tiny best-seller note or a pink allergen tag. No prices and no boxes.

Deep burgundy. The left two-thirds is an interactive map restyled entirely in burgundy and pink with rounded corners, the script logo as its pin and a small address card overlaid bottom-left. The right third is a rounded outlined panel listing opening hours, phone and email under tiny capital labels, plus two social icons. The script logo, large and white, is centred below, followed by a tracked-capitals legal line.

steal: Set a headline with its first lines as outline strokes and the last line solid, so emphasis falls on the final phrase without a size change.
Replace the stock map with one restyled in the brand's two colours and use the logo as the pin.
Build the menu from small cut-out product photos beside bold names and italic notes in two columns, with no cards.

references.name: Humanoid Index
references.idea: A catalogue of humanoid robots as a single-screen instrument: spin a wheel of names and one specimen appears on a plain card, ready to compare.
references.hero: A white, app-like screen with no headline. Top centre: a small segmented pill control with three categories and grey counts. Dead centre: a pale-grey rounded card about 400 by 455px holding one cut-out robot; above its top-left, a tiny maker logo with name, year and company at 13px; below it, a pill toolbar of four line icons. To its right, a paler empty card with a plus button labelled 'Compare'. Left of the card, a vertical wheel of robot names: the selected one black at 20px, the rest shrinking, fading and tilting along an arc. At the far left, mid-height: a logo glyph, a grid toggle and two credit lines.
references.type: Geist Sans Regular only, between 12 and 20px with -0.04em tracking. Hierarchy comes from grey value and opacity rather than size or weight; the selected name at 20px is the largest text on the page. No display type at all.
references.colour: #ffffff #f9f9f9 #1c1c1c #9b9b9b #f1b80e — White page, off-white cards, black and grey text. All colour arrives through the robots themselves, such as one yellow model.
references.imagery: Cut-out product shots and renders of robots, full figure, centred with even padding on identical off-white rounded cards, held at one scale and stance so models compare like specimens. A grey two-blob skeleton shows while loading.
references.layout: One fixed viewport with no sections: centred card, compare slot to its right, name wheel to its left, controls parked at top centre and far left. Roughly 60% of the screen is empty white. Scrolling changes the selection, not the position.

sections.description: The index is a wheel picker rather than a grid: about nine names are stacked vertically to the left of the card, right-aligned on a shallow arc. The active name is full black at 20px; neighbours step down in size, fade to light grey and tilt progressively, as if on a drum. Scrolling rotates the drum and swaps the card image, and the line above the card updates with the maker's logo, year and company.

On mobile the layout becomes a horizontal card carousel: a white rounded card nearly the full viewport tall holds the robot, the next card peeks about 30px at the right, and a bottom sheet with a drag handle carries a maker icon, the model name at about 28px with the year in grey beside it, the company beneath and a position counter right-aligned.

steal: Replace a thumbnail grid with a vertical wheel of names whose items shrink, fade and tilt away from the selection.
Hold every catalogue item at the same scale and stance on an identical off-white card so differences read instantly.
Keep all text between 12 and 20px and build hierarchy from grey values, leaving the object as the only large thing on screen.

references.name: Aardvark Book Club
references.idea: A book club dressed as a sweet shop: fat black type, tumbling 3D books and boxes on wavy colour fields, annotated with handwritten asides.
references.hero: A saturated yellow field with two large wavy blobs, pale yellow then orange, rising from the bottom. A three-line headline in Champ Bold, black, at about 8.3vw with leading under 0.85, is flush to a 15px left margin and reaches 60% across. Beneath it: a four-line paragraph 310px wide and a magenta split button (label plus arrow square). Right of centre a 3D hardback in navy and pink tilts 20 degrees, 600px tall; another book is cropped by the top-left corner, a third by the bottom edge. A purple handwritten note sits rotated at far right. Nav: pale-yellow pill links centred, an orange login button, black round social icons.
references.type: Champ Bold, an ultra-heavy wide sans with a looped g, for headings at 120px with tight tracking and leading; Degular for 18px body and pill labels; a purple handwritten script (Hello Organichand) for rotated margin notes and step labels. Three distinct voices.
references.colour: #ffd249 #faed8f #f9a21f #ffdbfd #a4f6f8 #fd48f2 — Each section owns one flat candy colour: yellow hero, white shelf, pink steps, cyan unboxing, deep violet footer. Type stays black; buttons are magenta.
references.imagery: 3D-rendered hardbacks and a patterned shipping box, cut out and tilted, floating over flat wavy vector shapes; real book covers on tilted coloured cards; black line drawings of figures on step cards. Nothing sits square to the grid.
references.layout: Sections are full-width panels with roughly 80px corner radius inset about 20px from the viewport, each a different colour. Headings alternate left and centre; cards overlap and rotate a few degrees; handwritten notes are tucked beside headings at an angle.

sections.description: White band. A centred black heading at 5.5vw over a two-line subline, with a rotated handwritten note at its upper left. Below, a horizontal row of book covers, each on a rounded colour-matched card with a small tag pill at top-left; cards tilt alternately by 3 degrees at staggered heights, the last cropped by the right edge, with two round arrow buttons above at right. Later, covers give way to same-coloured info cards with genre pills, heavy title and blurb.

A pale-pink rounded panel with lighter wavy shapes inside. Heavy black heading at left with a handwritten aside beside it; a small round logo stamp and a magenta split button at right. Along the bottom, four portrait cards about 250px wide in cyan, magenta, yellow and violet overlap like a fanned hand, each rotated a few degrees, with a handwritten step label at top, a black line drawing in the middle and a heavy caption at the foot.

A full-viewport cyan rounded panel containing only a 3D shipping box wrapped in a wavy magenta, violet and black pattern, centred. Across the scroll it goes from closed and tilted to lid open, growing to about 57% of the viewport width, with a single handwritten note at its right. No heading and no button.

The preceding white section ends in large rounded bottom corners over a deep violet footer. Left: white logo, two store badges, two magenta round social icons. Centre: the patterned box again, cropped by the bottom edge. Right: a small heavy heading, a white rounded email field and a magenta split button. A black legal strip closes the page.

steal: Give each section one flat saturated colour inside a large-radius inset panel and keep the type black across all of them.
Add rotated handwritten margin notes beside headings to carry secondary facts in a second voice.
Fan step cards so they overlap and tilt instead of sitting in an even grid.
